skill.name: email-handler
skill.description: Create transactional email templates with React Email and integrate them with the project sendMail utility.
skill.summary: Build React Email templates and connect them to server-side transactional email sending.
skill.author: AayushBaniya2006

security_audit.summary: The skill has a legitimate but confirmed outbound email capability through sendMail integration. The external command alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, and the environment alert references a public app URL rather than secrets. The main security concern is missing guidance for recipient authorization and link validation before sending email.

remediation.issue: Outbound email sending can target arbitrary recipients if copied without safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Document authorization, consent, rate limits, and recipient validation before sendMail is called.

remediation.issue: Email templates accept dynamic action URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Require action URLs to come from appConfig or NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, and validate allowed domains before rendering buttons.

remediation.issue: The example uses a placeholder production URL.
remediation.suggestion: Replace placeholder URLs with configuration-driven examples and state that secrets must not be embedded in templates.

content.value_statement: Transactional email work often needs consistent templates, shared layouts, and reliable delivery hooks. This skill guides React Email templates, rendering, and sendMail integration.
actual_capabilities: Creates React Email templates under src/emails.
Uses a shared Layout component with preview text.
Shows how to render templates to HTML with React Email.
Integrates sendMail calls in API routes or server actions.
Uses appConfig and public app URLs for consistent branding and links.
limitations: It provides guidance and code patterns, not a managed email delivery service.
It relies on the host project having React Email, sendMail, and Layout available.
It does not verify deliverability, DNS records, or provider credentials.
It should not be used to send unsolicited or unapproved messages.

use_cases.title: Create Account Emails
use_cases.description: Build typed welcome, verification, and password reset emails that share the existing React Email layout.

use_cases.title: Add Server Sending Hooks
use_cases.description: Integrate rendered templates with sendMail inside API routes or server actions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Branded Notifications
use_cases.description: Keep transactional messages consistent with app colors, support addresses, and shared layout components.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Email
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React Email welcome template in src/emails. Use the shared Layout, typed props, and clear preview text.

prompt_templates.title: Add Sending Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Add server-side sending for my existing email template. Render it with React Email and call the project sendMail utility.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Notification Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this notification email flow for consistent layout, typed data, safe links, and correct server action placement.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Transactional Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the email templates and sending points for account verification, password reset, and billing notifications.

output_examples.input: Create a welcome email for new workspace members.
output: A typed React Email template using the shared Layout and preview text.
Clear dynamic fields for the member name, workspace name, and invitation link.
A short note on where the template should be rendered before sending.

output_examples.input: Add sending logic after a password reset token is created.
output_examples.output: The result explains where to render the reset email, how to call sendMail, and which recipient and link checks should run first.
The result describes shared layout usage, typed billing props, consistent brand settings, and a server-side send point.

best_practices: Use one shared Layout and previewText on every template.
Validate recipients and action URLs before sending messages.
Use appConfig and public base URL settings for brand data and links.
anti_patterns: Sending email from user-controlled inputs without authorization checks.
Hardcoding production URLs, support emails, or brand values in each template.
Building templates without typed props or preview text.

faq.question: What framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets React Email templates in a TypeScript or Next.js style project.

faq.question: Can it send emails by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides code that uses the project sendMail utility and existing email provider setup.

faq.question: Does it include email provider configuration?
faq.answer: No. Provider credentials, DNS records, and deliverability setup remain outside this skill.

faq.question: How should links be built?
faq.answer: Use configured app URLs and validate allowed domains before adding links to templates.

faq.question: Can it update existing email templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can align existing templates with the shared Layout, typed props, and branding config.

faq.question: Is it safe for marketing email campaigns?
faq.answer: It is designed for transactional messages. Campaign sending needs consent, unsubscribe, and compliance controls.
